thread:
Megan: quick design check — i'm trying a tiny change: when you open a route analytics page we auto-apply a per-route default filter (model pinned + last 7d). thinking we should surface the telemetry sampling rate in the UI and decide whether that sampling info is saved/exported with queries. thoughts? :thinking:

Raj: share the prototype? my concern is users saving a view that silently uses sampled telemetry and later wondering why results don't match raw exports.

Megan: proto here: https://redwood.tools/proto/route-defaults-v2. current mock shows a micro-badge next to filters: "telemetry: sampled 10%" and the save/export modal has a checkbox "include sampling metadata" (checked by default).

Tobias: i'm in favor of explicit exposure. API question: do we persist sampling inline in the saved query or as a ref pointer to a sampling config? inline is easy but hard to change later.

Sierra: prefer a pointer: saved_query.telemetry_ref -> "projects/123/sampling-configs/alpha". lets us update sampling policies without rewriting saved queries.

Raj: for exports (notably notebook exports) we need reproducibility. even if saved_query stores a pointer, export payload should resolve that pointer into a concrete snapshot (pct, seed, policy_version) so notebooks can reproduce exact rows.

Megan: agreed. UX plan: show badge with hover text "Resolved sampling: v4 — 10% (exports include seed & snapshot)". Save modal will store the pointer and a flag include_sampling_metadata=true. Exports always include resolved snapshot fields.

Tobias: API sketch (pseudo):

```
POST /api/v1/saved_queries
{
  "name": "latency-by-model",
  "scope": "route:rt-900",
  "filters": {"model":"rw-lite-1","since":"7d"},
  "telemetry_ref": "sampling-configs/alpha",
  "include_sampling_metadata": true
}

GET /api/v1/saved_queries/:id/export?format=notebook
// response.export_snapshot -> { pct: 0.1, seed: 912387, policy_id: "alpha", snapshot_id: "snap-2026-03-01" }
```

Sierra: one nuance — if a user drills from route -> model breakdown and clicks save, that save should capture the drill-in scope (model-level) rather than the route default. Save modal copy should clarify scope: "Save current (model) view" vs "Save route default".

Megan: good catch. also need to think quotas: full-resolution export might consume significant export quota. modal should show estimated rows & quota cost and offer a fallback: "sampled export (fast, cheaper)" or "full export (queued, uses X quota)". default to sampled to avoid surprises.

Raj: from a policy side, workspace-level export permissions should gate full exports. if user lacks quota, modal should disable full export and explain alternatives.

Tobias: infra/telemetry note: every export that resolves sampling should create an audit entry linking export_job_id <-> snapshot_id so compliance teams can trace exact reproducibility. include seed in the export payload.

Megan: proposed action items:
- Sierra: write modal copy + badge tooltip + drill-in language (design) — due Wed EOD
- Tobias: open API PR with saved_queries shape (pointer + export snapshot) and export audit fields — stubbing now
- Raj: add quota callout + sampled/full export fallback UI in modal — will pair with devex
- Megan: record short walkthrough video and update prototype link for PMs

ConsoleBot: Megan pinned a message: "route defaults + export sampling" :pushpin:

Sierra: i'll author a short spec in product/ with an examples matrix (route-default, route->model drill-in, global). will ping eng + devex for early review.

Raj: tiny opt: add a user preference "Always include sampling metadata in exports" to reduce modal friction for power users. also emit analytics events for saved_query.created with telemetry_ref and include_sampling_metadata flag.

Tobias: agree on the pref. infra will ensure resolved exports write snapshot_id to audit and return snapshot meta in export response.

Megan: thanks team — closing this Slack thread, will reopen with spec link & API PR. I will follow up with updated prototype. :raised_hands:
